question: Is the judge model a commodity or a structural choice? Compare Jev against general-purpose LLM judges on five axes, not just accuracy.

fixture.question: contracts/questions.v1.json relation criteria, verbatim for every judge

axes.accuracy: mean label agreement with gold across runs
axes.stability: fraction of pairs whose label differs across runs (unstable pair rate); lower is better
axes.calibration: binary Brier score on p(contradiction) vs gold, mean across runs; lower is better
axes.schema_reliability: fraction of responses that parse into a valid labelled probability distribution

gates.judge_is_commodity: deepseek (either model) has mean accuracy >= jev AND unstable-pair rate <= jev AND parse-failure rate <= jev
gates.jev_structural_advantage: jev has strictly lower unstable-pair rate OR strictly lower parse-failure rate OR strictly lower Brier with comparable accuracy
gates.decision: commodity -> swap the judge, keep the pipeline (this is itself proof that the architecture is model-independent). structural advantage -> record which axes and by how much.

prohibited_after_freeze: changing the fixture, gold labels, or the question
dropping the v4-pro arm after seeing flash results
limitations: DeepSeek probabilities are self-reported, not trained-calibrated; the Brier comparison is generous to them only if their confidence is honest.
Latency depends on network location; the absolute numbers are less meaningful than the ratio.
Cost is reported as token counts; only Jev pricing is verified.
